title: Incident Prioritization and Capacity Evidence Manifest
author: Maya Lin
body:
Summary
======

This page defines the Incident Prioritization and Capacity Evidence Manifest: a concise, reproducible rubric that engineers, oncall responders, and SRE tooling use to (1) score incidents for prioritization, (2) determine pre-approved capacity actions, and (3) produce a complete evidence bundle for post-incident review. The goal is to reduce subjective decisions during high-pressure incidents and to accelerate capacity-safe remediation.

When to use this manifest
------------------------
- Any multi-tenant or service-impacting event where SLO burn exceeds 3% in a 15-minute window.
- Any sustained latency tail (p95 -> p99.9 delta > 2x expected range for 30+ minutes).
- Any unexpected backend OOMs, queue growth, or cold-start cascades affecting routing/throughput.

Primary outcomes
----------------
1. A numeric incident priority (P0, P1, P2, P3) computed via evidence scoring.
2. A capacity action recommendation: NO_ACTION / SOFT_SCALE / HARD_SCALE / THROTTLE / EVICT.
3. A structured evidence bundle (telemetry, traces, sample requests, config snapshot) saved to the incident record.

Evidence types and weights (manifest table)
-------------------------------------------
The manifest uses a weighted scoring system. Evidence items are collected automatically where possible and manually validated by the responder. Scores are additive; thresholds map to a priority and to allowed capacity actions.

| Evidence type | Short id | Weight | Required for P0? | Notes |
|---------------|---------:|-------:|:----------------:|-------|
| SLO burn rate (15m) | slo15 | 40 | Yes | Measured as percentage points above baseline; baseline=expected 15m burn.
| Error surge (5m) | err5 | 25 | Yes | Rate of 5xx per 1k requests vs baseline.
| Tail latency delta | tail | 20 | Yes | p99.9 - p95 relative delta, normalized to expected tail.
| Queue length growth | qlen | 10 | No | Percent growth in service incoming queue over 10m.
| OOM or resource faults | oom | 30 | Yes | Boolean; if true, treat as hard signal.
| Traffic imbalance (region) | region | 8 | No | Delta of traffic routed to region vs median.
| Config change in last 30m | cfg | 15 | No | Link to change-id and diff.
| Canary evaluation failures | can | 20 | No | Failing canary checks for model or infra rollouts.
| Customer-impact reports | cust | 12 | No | Verified customer complaint count in last 30m.
| Synthetic canary failures | synth | 12 | No | From synthetic probes; include run id.

Scoring algorithm
-----------------
1. Gather available evidence and compute a total score = sum(weight * normalized_value). For boolean signals (OOM, config change) normalized_value is 1 if true, 0 otherwise. For proportion signals (slo15, err5, tail) normalized_value is a capped ratio: min(1, observed / threshold).
2. Normalize total_score to a 0-100 scale for mapping. Example mapping (tunable):
   - 75+ -> P0 (Immediate incident; pre-approved hard-capacity + mitigation).
   - 50-74 -> P1 (High; soft-scale + targeted throttles).
   - 30-49 -> P2 (Medium; routing adjustments + cache priming).
   - <30 -> P3 (Investigate; no aggressive capacity changes).

Capacity action mapping (policy)
-------------------------------
- P0: HARD_SCALE allowed (provision reserved nodes or burst capacity), EVICT allowed (tenant eviction on authorization), immediate rollback of recent config/rollout if cfg or can are true. Throttle policies may be applied only after scaling if scaling fails.
- P1: SOFT_SCALE recommended (warm pool expansion, increase concurrent slots by up to 30%), targeted THROTTLE for heavy tenants, enable additional batching or KV-prefetch caches.
- P2: NO_ACTION / ROUTE_ADJUST recommended (shift traffic within region), enable non-disruptive cache refresh.
- P3: INVESTIGATE; capture evidence and follow up.

Pre-approval matrix and guardrails
---------------------------------
- Engineering managers for affected services pre-authorize per-service burst limits and eviction tolerance in the service manifest. See service manifest key fields: "burst_limit_nodes", "eviction_allowed", "priority_tenants".
- Hard_scale actions must be invoked by a responder with role: "sre-lead" or via automation if score >= 85. Manual hard scale requires an entry in the incident comments with change-id and expected rollback window.
- Eviction for multi-tenant isolation requires sign-off from product on call or SRE director unless eviction is for a single tenant producing >50% of SLO burn.

Example CLI snippets and API calls
---------------------------------
- Retrieve 15m SLO burn: curl -sS \"https://telemetry.internal/api/v1/slo/burn?srv=MODEL-SERVING&window=15m\" | jq '.burn'
- Request soft-scale: rscale --service MODEL-SERVING --type soft --percent 25 --reason "P1 soft-scale auto-recommendation"
- Trigger eviction (automated, limited): evict-tenant --service MODEL-SERVING --tenant-id tenant-42 --grace 120 --auth-token $SRE_TOKEN
- Capture evidence bundle: incident-cli evidence capture --incident $INC_ID --include traces,metrics,config --output s3://inc-bundles/$INC_ID.tar.gz

Evidence bundle contents (required)
-----------------------------------
Every incident record where score >= 30 must have an evidence bundle attached with the following files/links:
- metrics.json (15m and 5m aggregations for latency, errors, qlen)
- top-traces.json (top 50 traces by duration and error)
- sample-requests.log (up to 200 anonymized requests with headers and latencies)
- config-diff.patch (git diff for services changed in last 30m) or "no-conf-changes" marker
- autoscale-actions.log (any autoscaling or scale requests made during the incident)
- routing-snapshot.json (live routing table and policies)

Incident playbook (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1. Detection & initial score (first 5 minutes):
   a. Pager fires or synthetic indicates failure. Open incident with template "capacity-evidence-manifest".
   b. Run automated evidence-collector (incident-cli evidence capture --quick). Collector fills initial values for slo15, err5, tail, qlen, region.
   c. Compute initial score and annotate incident: /incident annotate --score 72 --reason "slo15=0.8, err5=0.6, oom=0".
2. Triage (5-20 minutes):
   a. Identify owner service and run runbook: runbook exec service-owner-checklist.
   b. If score >= 75, escalate to SRE lead and consider HARD_SCALE via automation if pre-approval exists.
   c. If OOM detected (oom=1), prioritize memory stabilization: reduce concurrency, disable largest batchers, apply config rollback if recent change present.
3. Containment & mitigation (20-60 minutes):
   a. Apply recommended capacity action. Document commands and expected effect.
   b. Apply targeted throttles for heavy tenants: throttle --tenant tenant-42 --rate 0.2 --duration 30m.
   c. If scaling is constrained, apply graceful degradation routes (modes: short-responses, stubbed embeddings, reduced beam width).
4. Recovery verification (60+ minutes):
   a. Confirm SLO burn rate is decreasing over three consecutive 5m windows.
   b. Roll back temporary throttles and verify stability for 30 minutes before full rollback of scaling.
5. Evidence finalization & severity confirmation:
   a. Ensure evidence bundle is attached.
   b. Confirm final priority and enter remediation tasks (owner, ETA, MTTD, MTR).

Post-incident review requirements
--------------------------------
- If final priority was P0 or P1, convene a 1-hour postmortem within 5 business days. Required deliverables: timeline, evidence bundle link, root cause hypothesis, mitigation plan, owners, and scheduled follow-up (calendar invite).
- Postmortem must score the original incident scoring accuracy (was the computed score predictive of severity?). Include a short retro on thresholds and weight tuning.

Operational tooling integration points
-------------------------------------
- Telemetry pipeline: evidence-collector plugin must be wired into the SLO pipeline (namespace: slo.compute.v1). It provides slo15 and err5 signals.
- Incident CLI: incident-cli must implement automatic capture hooks for traces and metrics and produce the evidence bundle described above.
- Autoscale API: rscale service must accept signed requests from incident automation with a TTL and rollback hint. Every scale request must be logged to autoscale-actions.log and surfaced in the incident UI.
- Eviction service: evict-tenant must implement a dry-run mode and an audit webhook to record approvals.

Ownership and governance
------------------------
- Service owners (on-call rotation): ensure service manifest contains burst limits and eviction policy.
- SRE tooling team: maintain incident-cli, evidence-collector, and rscale integrations.
- SRE leads: authority to approve hard scale and eviction during P0 events per the pre-approval matrix.

Tuning playbook and cadence
---------------------------
- Quarterly review: the weights in the manifest and the score->priority mapping are reviewed end of quarter by SRE tooling + service leads. Adjust thresholds based on incident history and cost/availability tradeoffs.
- After a P0 incident: immediately convene a calibration session to test the score against the incident timeline and update weights if false positives/negatives occurred.

Appendices
---------
A. Example metrics.json snippet
{
  "service": "MODEL-SERVING",
  "window": "15m",
  "slo_burn_pct": 7.3,
  "error_rate_per_k": 4.2,
  "p95": 210,
  "p99_9": 980
}

B. Change approval template (for manual hard scale)
- Incident ID: {INC_ID}
- Requested action: HARD_SCALE + burst 20 nodes
- Justification: sudden p99.9 tail and OOMs in worker pool
- Expected rollback window: 120 minutes
- Approver: {SRE_LEAD}

C. Quick checklist for post-incident evidence verification
- [ ] metrics.json attached and matches incident timeline
- [ ] top-traces.json includes representative errors
- [ ] config diff attached or explicit marker present
- [ ] autoscale-actions.log present and annotated
- [ ] routing-snapshot captures the time-of-incident routes

If anything on this page conflicts with a service manifest (stored in service-configs repo), the service manifest takes precedence for burst limits and eviction policies.

For questions or tooling requests, contact the SRE tooling team (sre-tooling@redwood.ai) or open a ticket in the SRE queue.
